Lenzing AG shareholders approved a roughly €300 million (~$349.8 million) capital increase to strengthen its balance sheet and support the “Grow Nonwovens, Reset Textiles” strategy.
The issue is due by February 25, 2027, with terms to be set by management.
Major shareholders backed the move, while Martin Seiter joined the Supervisory Board.

title: WILEYTEX ecoloration targets Scope 3 emissions in cotton dyeing
summary:
WILEYTEX’s ecoloration technology targets Scope 3 emissions at the dye-house level, cutting carbon and energy use by 80 per cent and water use by up to 90 per cent.
The salt-free, steam-free cotton dyeing process also reduces dye consumption by about 20 per cent.
Commercial deployment in Eswatini provides production-level data for supply-chain reporting

title: China’s central bank to conduct overnight reverse repos from Aug 27
summary:
China’s central bank will conduct overnight reverse repo operations from August 27 to September 1 to address short-term banking-system liquidity needs. 
The fixed-rate, quantity-based operations will be capped at 600 billion yuan daily. 
Introduced in June, the tool is intended to smooth temporary liquidity fluctuations, improve liquidity-management efficiency and diversify monetary policy.

title: UK productivity grows 1.1% in two years to Q2 2026: Report
summary:
UK productivity appears to be recovering, with administrative data showing output per hour rising 1.1 per cent annually in the two years to Q2 2026 after a 0.7 per cent decline previously. 
The improvement was broad-based across sectors and driven mainly by slower growth in hours worked, though productivity remains well below its pre-pandemic path.

title: What drove Germany’s GDP growth in Q2 2026?
summary:
Germany's GDP rose 0.3 per cent quarter on quarter in Q2 2026, with exports again the main growth driver.
Exports rose 2.0 per cent, led by a 2.6 per cent increase in goods exports, while manufacturing value added grew 0.9 per cent. 
Wholesale and retail turnover also exceeded expectations, although machinery and equipment investment fell 1.4 per cent.

title: Kenya pushes harmonised standards to remove barriers to African trade
summary:
Kenya’s standards agency says African nations should harmonise trade regulations, with intra-African commerce at just 16 per cent.
For exporters and manufacturers, fragmented rules and conflicting national standards add friction to cross-border goods movement.
Delegates from 44 African nations are discussing technical trade barriers at ARSO’s five-day Mombasa summit.

title: EU goods imports outpace exports in Q2 2026
summary:
EU goods trade swung to a €21.8 billion (~$25.3 billion) deficit in Q2 2026 as imports from non-EU countries exceeded exports.
Imports rose 9.9 per cent quarter on quarter, faster than the 5.4 per cent export increase, affecting trade planning.
Energy, raw materials and other manufactured goods drove the deficit, Eurostat data showed.

title: Moody’s affirms Philippines’ ‘Baa2’ credit rating, stable outlook
summary:
Moody’s Ratings has affirmed the Philippines’ ‘Baa2’ investment-grade rating and maintained its stable outlook, holding the country’s credit standing steady even as the latter navigates rising energy costs and a public infrastructure spending slowdown. 
It expects fiscal metrics to stabilise over two years, backed by a recovery in growth and the government’s continued commitment to fiscal consolidation.

title: India seeks Japanese capital for technology & manufacturing growth
summary:
India sought deeper investment ties with Japan as Piyush Goyal met leading financial institutions in Tokyo. 
Discussions covered long-term capital flows, regulatory predictability, profit repatriation and GIFT City’s role in cross-border investment. 
Japanese institutions expressed confidence in India’s growth prospects and highlighted opportunities in AI and advanced manufacturing.

title: Is supply tightness driving China's VSF price divergence?
summary:
VSF prices rose across August 14-24, with China domestic grades outpacing international benchmarks as local material shortages tightened supply.
High-end China domestic VSF gained 1.03 per cent and medium grade 0.62 per cent; 1.2D and 1.5D benchmarks rose only 0.32-0.33 per cent.
Further movement hinges on China supply normalisation and currently stable dissolving pulp and caustic soda costs.

title: New Zealand apparel imports up in July, but cumulative down
summary:
New Zealand’s apparel imports rose 0.8 per cent year on year to NZ$174.01 million (~$102 million) in July 2026, Stats NZ data show.
January–July imports fell 1.6 per cent to NZ$1.197 billion; knitted apparel declined 1 per cent and non-knitted 2.4 per cent.
Apparel exports fell 19.3 per cent in July but rose 1.1 per cent in January–July; knitted fabric imports rose 21.6 per cent cumulatively.

title: US apparel sourcing could shift to fewer, bigger strategic vendors
summary:
US fashion companies sourced apparel from 49 countries in 2026, up from 46 in 2025, but only 21.1 per cent expect to add countries.
TexPro says US HS 61 and 62 apparel imports fell 7.77 per cent to $36.90 billion in H1 2026.
Some 47.4 per cent plan fewer suppliers as buyers seek stronger vendors with traceability, compliance, speed and multi-country options.

title: $3.1 bn lost; inside the shift at 30 US fashion companies
summary:
TexPro shows US HS 61 and HS 62 imports fell 7.77 per cent year on year to about $36.90 billion in January-June 2026.
China and India lost nearly $2.98 billion, while gains by Vietnam, Cambodia and Indonesia totalled only about $407 million.
USFIA respondents sourced from 49 countries, but 47.4 per cent expect to use fewer suppliers as tariff risk reshapes sourcing.

title: Sweden’s apparel imports fall as China strengthens market share
summary:
Sweden’s apparel imports fell 2.6 per cent year on year to $2.422 billion in H1 2026, but Asian suppliers strengthened their position.
China’s shipments rose 5.8 per cent to $447.859 million, lifting its share to 18.48 per cent, while Bangladesh retained second place.
Denmark, Germany and Poland posted double-digit declines; cotton and trousers and shorts led fibre and product categories.

title: Australia's City Chic's FY26 EBITDA surges 92% on margin
summary:
City Chic Collective's FY26 underlying EBITDA rose 92 per cent to A$12.3 million, while trading margin reached 60.6 per cent.
ANZ revenue grew 7.6 per cent, but US sales fell as tariff uncertainty prompted lower purchasing and pressured partner sales.
FY27 starts with stronger ANZ stores and improving US momentum, backed by lower costs, leaner inventory and undrawn debt capacity.

title: Can Bangladesh’s $38.7 bn RMG sector withstand 100+ mill shutdown
summary:
More than 100 textile factories in Narsingdi have stopped or severely curtailed production, while BTMA says over 900 member mills nationwide are shut.
TexPro data shows China supplied 89.5 per cent of Bangladesh’s selected knitted-fabric imports in January–May 2026.
RMG exports reached $38.70 billion in FY2025-26, but August outages may test lead times and local value addition.

title: Egypt's apparel boom faces a new test: Can growth diversify?
summary:
Egypt’s apparel exports rose 15 per cent to $1.775 billion in H1 2026, with June shipments up 47 per cent year on year to $355 million.
The US and Europe added $229 million, slightly more than the sector’s total $227 million gain, while other destinations were slightly negative.
AEC targets up to $4 billion in 2026 as new textile and apparel capacity tests whether growth can diversify.

title: Canada’s Roots goes private in Marquee deal to drive global growth
summary:
Marquee Brands will acquire Roots via JM&A, taking the Canadian lifestyle brand private while keeping its Toronto headquarters.
JM&A will run design, development, manufacturing, distribution, retail and e-commerce for menswear and womenswear in Canada and the US.
Shareholders are offered C$4.10 per share, a 36 per cent premium; vote is due in October 2026, with closing targeted for Q4 2026.

title: Argentina’s apparel imports surge 36% as liberalisation lowers prices
summary:
Argentina’s apparel import value rose 36.0 per cent year on year to $419.38 million in H1 2026, with volume at 28.45 million kg. 
Lower clothing duties under Decree 236/2025, eased import controls, better foreign currency access and cross-border e-commerce boosted overseas sourcing. 
T-shirts, jerseys and trousers grew faster than coats, while the average import price fell to $14.74 per kg.

title: Could Kenya become Egypt’s gateway to a wider African market?
summary:
Africa’s young, urbanising consumer base is creating sustained demand for apparel and footwear. 
Egypt’s ECAHT has agreed to set up a logistics hub in Kenya to reduce freight costs, delivery times and distributor access barriers. 
The hub will cover shipping, warehousing and insurance, with shipments due in September and targeted garment exports estimated to rise by at least 20 per cent.
